930	/**
931	 * Projects the persisted graph state onto the pinned definition. Precedence per node: a task error is failed, an
932	 * interrupt is awaiting approval, confirmed completion evidence is succeeded (verification nodes additionally need
933	 * their registered packet to load, match its hash and have passed), then the last persisted event, then pending.
934	 * The run succeeds only once integrated with nothing pending; contradictory evidence is paused.
935	 */
936	export function projectSnapshot(scope: Scope, definition: WorkflowDefinition, state: RunExport, rawEvents: readonly RawEvent[], packets: readonly LoadedPacket[], map: LaneMap = laneMap(LEGACY_LANES)): RunSnapshot {
937	  const lastEvent = new Map<string, RawEvent>()
938	  const eventAttempt = new Map<string, number>()
939	  for (const event of rawEvents) {
940	    const node = eventNode(definition, event.node, map)
941	    if (!node) continue
942	    // Only a status-bearing event moves a node; a plain record (`stopped`, a note) never hides the last status.
943	    if (EVENT_STATUS[event.status] !== undefined) lastEvent.set(node, event)
944	    const attempt = attemptFromMessage(event.message)
945	    if (attempt !== null) eventAttempt.set(node, Math.max(attempt, eventAttempt.get(node) ?? 0))
946	  }
947	  const latestPacket = (phase: 'worker' | 'candidate', worker: string) => packets
948	    .filter(packet => packet.phase === phase && packet.node_id === worker).sort((a, b) => b.attempt - a.attempt)[0]
949	  const workers = new Set(packets.map(packet => packet.node_id))
950	  const nodes = definition.nodes.map(node => {
951	    const task = state.tasks.find(candidate => candidate.node_id === node.node_id)
952	    const evidenced = map.workerOf.has(node.node_id) || node.node_id in TAIL_EVIDENCE_KEY
953	    const worker = map.workerOf.get(node.node_id)
954	    const workerPacket = worker ? latestPacket('worker', worker) : undefined
955	    let attempt = 0
956	    let session_id: string | null = null
957	    let result_uri: string | null = null
958	    if (worker) {
959	      if (workerPacket) {
960	        attempt = map.verifyNodes.has(node.node_id) ? workerPacket.attempt : 1
961	        result_uri = resultRoute(scope, state.run_id, 'worker', worker, workerPacket.attempt)
962	        const session = workerPacket.ok ? workerPacket.result.session_id : null
963	        session_id = typeof session === 'string' && session.length > 0 ? session : null
964	      }
965	      if (!map.verifyNodes.has(node.node_id)) {
966	        const receipt = laneValue(state.values, worker, 'launch')
967	        const session = receipt && typeof receipt === 'object' ? (receipt as Record<string, unknown>).session_id : null
968	        if (typeof session === 'string' && session.length > 0) session_id = session
969	      }
970	    }
971	    if (node.node_id === 'candidate') attempt = Math.max(0, ...packets.filter(packet => packet.phase === 'candidate').map(packet => packet.attempt))
972	    if (map.verifyNodes.has(node.node_id)) attempt = Math.max(attempt, eventAttempt.get(node.node_id) ?? 0)
973	    // The review node names its reviewer and links to the recorded result only from the export's review section, never from `values`.
974	    if (node.node_id === 'review' && state.review) {
975	      attempt = state.review.attempt
976	      session_id = redactPaths(state.review.reviewer_session_id)
977	      result_uri = reviewRoute(scope, state.run_id, state.review.attempt)
978	    }
979	    let status: NodeStatus
980	    const event = lastEvent.get(node.node_id)
981	    const eventStatus = event ? EVENT_STATUS[event.status] ?? null : null
982	    if (task?.error) status = 'failed'
983	    else if (task && task.interrupts.length > 0) status = 'awaiting_approval'
984	    else if (hasEvidence(state, node.node_id, map)) {
985	      if (map.verifyNodes.has(node.node_id)) status = workerPacket?.ok && workerPacket.gate.status === 'passed' ? 'succeeded' : 'paused'
986	      else if (node.node_id === 'candidate') {
987	        const latest = [...workers].map(candidate => latestPacket('candidate', candidate)).filter(packet => packet !== undefined)
988	        status = latest.length > 0 && latest.every(packet => packet.ok && packet.gate.status === 'passed') ? 'succeeded' : 'paused'
989	      } else status = 'succeeded'
990	    } else if (eventStatus === 'succeeded') status = evidenced ? 'paused' : 'succeeded'
991	    else if (eventStatus) status = eventStatus
992	    else status = 'pending'
993	    if (status !== 'pending' && attempt === 0) attempt = 1
994	    if (status === 'pending') { attempt = 0; session_id = null; result_uri = null }
995	    // The combined candidate holds one verified result per lane; link each so its evidence (screenshots included) is reachable.
996	    const lane_results = node.node_id === 'candidate' && status !== 'pending'
997	      ? map.lanes.flatMap(lane => {
998	        const packet = latestPacket('candidate', lane)
999	        return packet ? [{ worker: lane, attempt: packet.attempt, result_uri: resultRoute(scope, state.run_id, 'candidate', lane, packet.attempt) }] : []
1000	      })
1001	      : []
1002	    return { node_id: node.node_id, kind: node.kind, depends_on: [...node.depends_on], status, attempt, session_id, result_uri, lane_results }
1003	  })
1004	  const statuses = new Set(nodes.map(node => node.status))
1005	  const integrated = hasEvidence(state, 'integrate', map)
1006	  let status: NodeStatus
1007	  if (statuses.has('failed')) status = 'failed'
1008	  else if (statuses.has('awaiting_approval')) status = 'awaiting_approval'
1009	  else if (statuses.has('paused')) status = 'paused'
1010	  else if (integrated && state.next.length === 0 && !statuses.has('running') && !statuses.has('pending')) status = 'succeeded'
1011	  else if (integrated) status = 'paused'
1012	  else if (statuses.has('running') || state.next.length > 0) status = 'running'
1013	  else if (statuses.size === 1 && statuses.has('pending')) status = 'pending'
1014	  else status = 'paused'
1015	  return { contract_version: '1.0.0', run_id: state.run_id, status, last_sequence: rawEvents.at(-1)?.sequence ?? 0, nodes }
1016	}

1018	/** Publishes a verified packet's result: scoped artifact links, no worktree paths, and a failed status when the gate did not pass. */
1019	function projectWorkerResult(scope: Scope, runId: string, nodeId: string, packet: LoadedPacket & { ok: true }): WorkerResult {
1020	  const raw = packet.result
1021	  if (raw.run_id !== runId || raw.node_id !== packet.node_id || raw.attempt !== packet.attempt) {
1022	    throw new ProjectApiError(500, 'EVIDENCE_MISMATCH', 'The verification packet result does not match its registration.')
1023	  }
1024	  const passed = packet.gate.status === 'passed'
1025	  const checks = Array.isArray(raw.checks) ? (raw.checks as Record<string, unknown>[]).map(check => ({ ...check, cwd: `verification/${packet.phase}/${packet.node_id}/${packet.attempt}/worktree` })) : raw.checks
1026	  const artifacts = Array.isArray(raw.artifacts) ? (raw.artifacts as Record<string, unknown>[]).map(artifact => ({
1027	    ...artifact, uri: typeof artifact.artifact_id === 'string' ? `${runRoute(scope, runId)}/artifacts/${encodeURIComponent(artifact.artifact_id)}` : artifact.uri,
1028	  })) : raw.artifacts
1029	  const assumptions = Array.isArray(raw.open_assumptions) ? raw.open_assumptions.filter(item => typeof item === 'string' && item.trim().length > 0) : raw.open_assumptions
1030	  const candidate = {
1031	    contract_version: '1.0.0', run_id: runId, node_id: nodeId, attempt: packet.attempt, session_id: raw.session_id,
1032	    status: passed ? raw.status : 'failed', base_commit: raw.base_commit, output_commit: raw.output_commit,
1033	    changed_files: raw.changed_files, checks, open_assumptions: assumptions, artifacts,
1034	    ...(packet.deferred.length > 0 ? { deferred_checks: packet.deferred } : {}),
1035	    summary: typeof raw.summary === 'string' ? redactPaths(raw.summary) : raw.summary,
1036	    error: passed ? raw.error : { code: 'VERIFICATION_BLOCKED', message: redactPaths(packet.gate.reasons.join('; ')) || 'Verification did not pass.', retryable: true },
1037	  }
1038	  try {
1039	    return validateWorkerResult(candidate)
1040	  } catch (error) {
1041	    throw new ProjectApiError(500, 'RESULT_INVALID', `The verification packet result does not conform to the worker result contract: ${error instanceof z.ZodError ? issueText(error) : (error as Error).message}`)
1042	  }
1043	}

173	    ['absolute owned path', inputs => { inputs.workers[0].owned_paths = ['/etc'] }],
174	    ['traversal owned path', inputs => { inputs.workers[0].owned_paths = ['src/../..'] }],
175	    ['unconfirmed stop with a time', inputs => { inputs.workers[0].stop = { stopped: false, confirmed_at: '2026-01-01T12:20:00Z' } }],
176	    ['no workers', inputs => { inputs.workers = [] }],
177	    ['blank completion summary', inputs => { inputs.workers[0].completion!.summary = '' }],
178	    ['offset timestamp', inputs => { inputs.workers[0].launch!.launch_requested_at = '2026-01-01T12:00:00+00:00' }],
179	    ['unknown transport', inputs => { (inputs.automatic as Record<string, unknown>).reviewer_transport = 'manual' }],
180	  ]
181	  for (const [label, mutate] of cases) {
182	    const inputs = structuredClone(examples.runInputs)
183	    mutate(inputs)
184	    assert.throws(() => validateRunInputs(inputs), label)
185	  }
186	})

1	"""Reusable policy/evidence gates. No agents, browsers, shells or graph launches.
2	
3	Inputs must come from a trusted verifier plus backend-owned artifact registry, not
4	unchecked agent prose. Passing this evidence gate never authorizes integration.
5	"""
6	from __future__ import annotations
7	
8	import hashlib
9	import json
10	import shlex
11	from datetime import datetime
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator, FormatChecker
15	from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
16	
17	CONTRACTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "contracts" / "workflow"
18	
19	
20	# Check kinds that only mean something on the whole application: a lane's build and browser
21	# suite compile against contracts and a server that another lane of the same run may be
22	# changing. The worker phase still runs and records them on the lane's isolated snapshot,
23	# but only the candidate phase, where every lane's work is combined, gates on them.
24	# Lane-local kinds (unit, contract, integration) gate in both phases.
25	DEFERRED_WORKER_KINDS = frozenset({"build", "browser"})
26	
27	
28	def validate_schema(name: str, value: dict) -> None:
29	    schema = json.loads((CONTRACTS / f"{name}.schema.json").read_text())
30	    Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=FormatChecker()).validate(value)
31	
32	
33	def policy_digest(policy: dict) -> str:
34	    """Canonical UTF-8 JSON: sorted keys, no whitespace, literal Unicode."""
35	    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(policy, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode()).hexdigest()
36	
37	
38	def safe_path(value: str) -> str:
39	    normalized = value.rstrip("/")
40	    if not normalized or normalized.startswith("/") or any(char in normalized for char in "\\:*?[]") or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in normalized.split("/")):
41	        raise ValueError(f"Not an exact repository-relative path/prefix: {value}")
42	    return normalized
43	
44	
45	def owns(path: str, prefix: str) -> bool:
46	    return path == prefix or path.startswith(prefix + "/")
47	
48	
49	def unique(items: list[dict], key: str) -> dict:
50	    result = {item[key]: item for item in items}
51	    if len(result) != len(items):
52	        raise ValueError(f"Duplicate {key}")
53	    return result
54	
55	
56	# Policies before 1.2.0 derived the required check kinds from the role; the export of an old run keeps them.
57	ROLE_REQUIRED_KINDS = {"frontend": ("build", "browser"), "backend": ("unit",)}
58	
59	
60	def required_kinds(policy: dict, worker: dict) -> list[str]:
61	    """The check kinds a lane must pass: declared from policy 1.2.0, derived from the role before."""
62	    if "required_check_kinds" in worker:
63	        return list(worker["required_check_kinds"])
64	    if policy.get("version") in {"1.0.0", "1.1.0"} and worker.get("role") in ROLE_REQUIRED_KINDS:
65	        return list(ROLE_REQUIRED_KINDS[worker["role"]])
66	    raise ValueError(f"{worker.get('node_id')} declares no required_check_kinds")
67	
68	
69	def validate_policy(policy: dict) -> dict:
70	    validate_schema("verification", policy)
71	    workers = unique(policy["workers"], "node_id")
72	    claimed = []
73	    for worker in workers.values():
74	        paths = [safe_path(path) for path in worker["owned_paths"]]
75	        for other_node, other_path in claimed:
76	            if any(owns(path, other_path) or owns(other_path, path) for path in paths):
77	                raise ValueError(f"Overlapping ownership: {worker['node_id']} and {other_node}")
78	        claimed.extend((worker["node_id"], path) for path in paths)
79	        checks = unique(worker["checks"], "id")
80	        if len({tuple(check["argv"]) for check in checks.values()}) != len(checks):
81	            raise ValueError("Each check needs a distinct command")
82	        kinds = {check["kind"] for check in checks.values()}
83	        required = set(required_kinds(policy, worker))
84	        if not required <= kinds:
85	            raise ValueError(f"{worker['node_id']} requires {sorted(required)} checks; missing {sorted(required - kinds)}")
86	        for check in checks.values():
87	            unique(check["scenarios"], "id")
88	            if (check["kind"] == "browser") != bool(check["scenarios"]):
89	                raise ValueError("Browser checks require named scenarios; other checks must not have scenarios")
90	    drill = policy.get("failure_drill")
91	    if drill and (drill["node_id"] not in workers or policy.get("max_verification_attempts", 3) < 2):
92	        raise ValueError("Failure drill requires a configured worker and at least two allowed verification attempts")
93	    return policy
94	
95	
96	def evaluate_worker(policy: dict, result: dict, evidence: dict, *, expected: dict,
97	                    artifact_root: Path, artifact_paths: dict[str, Path], enforce_ownership: bool = True,
98	                    phase: str = "candidate") -> dict:
99	    """Fail closed on absent, stale or inconsistent evidence.
100	
101	    `expected` is backend-owned: run_id, node_id, attempt, base_commit,
102	    output_commit and verification_cwd. Caller must freeze edits and independently
103	    derive the full Git diff/commit before invoking; this function cannot prove
104	    that an agent has reported all changed files.
105	
106	    In the `worker` phase, checks of a DEFERRED_WORKER_KINDS kind are verified for
107	    integrity (approved argv, worktree, timeout) and recorded, but their outcome does
108	    not gate; the returned `deferred_checks` names them. Every other phase gates on all.
109	    """
110	    reasons = []
111	    deferred = []
112	    try:
113	        validate_policy(policy)
114	        validate_schema("workerResult", result)
115	        validate_schema("verificationEvidence", evidence)
116	        workers = {worker["node_id"]: worker for worker in policy["workers"]}
117	        worker = workers[expected["node_id"]]
118	        for field in ("run_id", "node_id", "attempt", "base_commit", "output_commit"):
119	            if result[field] != expected[field]:
120	                raise ValueError(f"Worker result has stale/mismatched {field}")
121	        for field in ("run_id", "node_id", "attempt", "output_commit"):
122	            if evidence[field] != expected[field]:
123	                raise ValueError(f"Verification evidence has stale/mismatched {field}")
124	        if evidence["policy_sha256"] != policy_digest(policy):
125	            raise ValueError("Verification policy changed after evidence capture")
126	        if result["status"] != "succeeded" or result["output_commit"] is None or result["error"] is not None:
127	            raise ValueError("Worker did not produce a successful durable result")
128	        prefixes = [safe_path(path) for path in worker["owned_paths"]]
129	        for changed in result["changed_files"]:
130	            if enforce_ownership and not any(owns(safe_path(changed), prefix) for prefix in prefixes):
131	                reasons.append(f"Changed file outside ownership: {changed}")
132	        artifacts = unique(result["artifacts"], "artifact_id")
133	        root = artifact_root.resolve(strict=True)
134	        resolved = {}
135	        for artifact_id, artifact in artifacts.items():
136	            path = artifact_paths[artifact_id].resolve(strict=True)
137	            if not path.is_relative_to(root) or not path.is_file():
138	                raise ValueError(f"Artifact escapes registry root: {artifact_id}")
139	            with path.open("rb") as handle:
140	                digest = hashlib.file_digest(handle, "sha256").hexdigest()
141	            if digest != artifact["sha256"]:
142	                raise ValueError(f"Artifact hash mismatch: {artifact_id}")
143	            resolved[artifact_id] = path
144	        supplied = unique(evidence["checks"], "id")
145	        required = {check["id"]: check for check in worker["checks"]}
146	        if set(supplied) != set(required):
147	            raise ValueError("Required check evidence missing or contains unknown check IDs")
148	        indexes = [check["worker_check_index"] for check in supplied.values()]
149	        if len(set(indexes)) != len(indexes):
150	            raise ValueError("A command execution cannot satisfy multiple check IDs")
151	        if phase == "worker":
152	            deferred = sorted(check_id for check_id, check in required.items() if check["kind"] in DEFERRED_WORKER_KINDS)
153	        deferred_indexes = {supplied[check_id]["worker_check_index"] for check_id in deferred}
154	        for index, check in enumerate(result["checks"]):
155	            if artifacts.get(check["log_artifact_id"], {}).get("kind") != "log":
156	                reasons.append("Executed check is missing a log artifact")
157	            if datetime.fromisoformat(check["finished_at"]) < datetime.fromisoformat(check["started_at"]):
158	                reasons.append("Check finish precedes start")
159	            if check["exit_code"] != 0 and index not in deferred_indexes:
160	                reasons.append(f"Executed check failed: {check['command']}")
161	        for check_id, requirement in required.items():
162	            receipt = supplied[check_id]
163	            execution = result["checks"][receipt["worker_check_index"]]
164	            if execution["command"] != shlex.join(requirement["argv"]):
165	                reasons.append(f"{check_id}: executed command differs from approved argv")
166	            if Path(execution["cwd"]).resolve() != Path(expected["verification_cwd"]).resolve():
167	                reasons.append(f"{check_id}: wrong verification worktree")
168	            duration = (datetime.fromisoformat(execution["finished_at"]) - datetime.fromisoformat(execution["started_at"])).total_seconds()
169	            if duration > requirement["timeout_seconds"]:
170	                reasons.append(f"{check_id}: execution exceeded approved timeout")
171	            if check_id in deferred:
172	                continue  # Executed and recorded; the candidate phase gates on the outcome.
173	            if requirement["kind"] in {"unit", "browser", "integration", "contract"}:
174	                tests = receipt["tests"]
175	                if tests is None or tests["passed"] < 1 or tests["failed"] > 0:
176	                    reasons.append(f"{check_id}: no passing test evidence or failed tests")
177	            scenarios = unique(receipt["scenarios"], "id")
178	            if requirement["kind"] == "browser" and receipt["tests"] is not None and receipt["tests"]["passed"] < len(requirement["scenarios"]):
179	                reasons.append(f"{check_id}: fewer passing tests than required browser scenarios")
180	            if set(scenarios) != {scenario["id"] for scenario in requirement["scenarios"]}:
181	                reasons.append(f"{check_id}: missing/unknown browser scenarios")
182	            screenshot_ids = []
183	            for scenario in scenarios.values():
184	                artifact_id = scenario["screenshot_artifact_id"]
185	                if scenario["status"] != "passed":
186	                    reasons.append(f"{check_id}/{scenario['id']}: browser scenario did not pass")
187	                if artifact_id is None or artifacts.get(artifact_id, {}).get("kind") != "screenshot":
188	                    reasons.append(f"{check_id}/{scenario['id']}: screenshot required")
189	                    continue
190	                screenshot_ids.append(artifact_id)
191	                # Format sanity only, not proof of visual correctness/authenticity.
192	                with resolved[artifact_id].open("rb") as image:
193	                    header = image.read(24)
194	                if len(header) < 24 or header[:8] != b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" or header[12:16] != b"IHDR" or int.from_bytes(header[16:20], "big") == 0 or int.from_bytes(header[20:24], "big") == 0:
195	                    reasons.append(f"{check_id}/{scenario['id']}: expected a PNG screenshot")
196	            if len(set(screenshot_ids)) != len(screenshot_ids):
197	                reasons.append(f"{check_id}: each scenario needs a distinct screenshot artifact")
198	    except (ValueError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, OSError) as error:
199	        reasons.append(str(error))
200	    except ValidationError as error:
201	        reasons.append(error.message)
202	    return {"status": "blocked" if reasons else "passed", "reasons": reasons, "deferred_checks": deferred,
203	            "pending_gates": ["independent_review", "integration_approval"],
204	            "integration_allowed": False}
205

1	# Workflow CLI cheatsheet
2	
3	Every command below was taken from the argparse definitions in `workflow/pipeline.py`, `workflow/launch.py` and `workflow/interactive.py` after the worker-lanes slice (PRD_WORKER_LANES). Longer explanations live in [RUNBOOK.md](RUNBOOK.md) and [features/project-workflows/README.md](../features/project-workflows/README.md).
4	
5	Worker lanes come from the feature's configuration: `features/<f>/feature.json` (2.0.0) declares every lane with its task file, `features/<f>/policy.json` (1.2.0) gives each lane its role label, owned paths, checks and `required_check_kinds`. A run launches every declared lane or the subset named with `--workers`; `<lane>` below is any selected lane id.
6	
7	```bash
8	PY="$PWD/.venv/bin/python"                                   # controller interpreter, run from the repo root
9	RUN="$HOME/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>/<run-id>"   # run directory, always outside the repo
10	```
11	
12	Two entry points:
13	
14	| Entry point | Shape | Use |
15	| --- | --- | --- |
16	| `$PY -m workflow launch <feature> [flags]` | one command | prepare and start a committed feature |
17	| `$PY -m workflow <action> "$RUN" [flags]` | one action per call | every other pipeline step, status, recovery |
18	
19	Nothing launches a Claude session without `--live`. Nothing ever pushes or merges `main`.
20	
21	## 1. One-command launch
22	
23	```bash
24	$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --dry-run --automatic          # validate and print the commands, execute nothing
25	$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --live --automatic             # unattended run to a verified feature branch
26	$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --live                         # manual run with operator gates
27	$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --live --automatic --workers adapter   # only the named lanes; the rest stay off-limits
28	```
29	
30	| Flag | Meaning | Default |
31	| --- | --- | --- |
32	| `<feature>` | a directory under `features/` listed in `FEATURES` in `workflow/launch.py` | required |
33	| `--run-id ID` | opaque run identifier, not a path | `<feature>-001` |
34	| `--run-root DIR` | run storage outside the repository | `~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>` |
35	| `--workers a,b` | launch only these declared lanes (unknown ids, duplicates and an empty list are refused before any Git action); the selection is pinned in `plan.json` | every declared lane |
36	| `--live` | authorize Claude usage | off |
37	| `--automatic` | run-scoped permission bypass for workers, automatic freeze, checks, native reviewer, verified feature branch | off, manual gates |
38	| `--worker-timeout-seconds N` | per-worker deadline from launch to completion signal, automatic only | 4 h, max 24 h |
39	| `--review-timeout-seconds N` | reviewer deadline from its launch to its completion file, automatic only | 30 min, max 24 h |
40	| `--reviewer-transport native\|print` | attachable reviewer session, or headless `claude --print`, automatic only | `native` |
41	| `--no-herdr` | omit terminal attachments | attaches |
42	| `--dry-run` | validate the feature configuration and print the commands | off |
43	
44	`launch` refuses an existing run directory. It runs, in order: `preflight`, `git switch -c <branch_prefix>/<run-id>`, `prepare`, `start`, and with `--automatic` also `automatic`. A `feature.json` still at version 1.0.0 (`ui_task`/`adapter_task`) is translated to the 2.0.0 shape and a deprecation line is printed; `--dry-run` lists it under `notes`. A policy `failure_drill` that names a lane the selection leaves out is skipped, with a note and a timeline event.
45	
46	## 2. Step-by-step pipeline (what `launch` runs for you)
47	
48	```bash
49	$PY -m workflow preflight "$RUN" --repo "$PWD" --policy features/<f>/policy.json --herdr [--automatic]
50	$PY -m workflow prepare   "$RUN" --repo "$PWD" --policy features/<f>/policy.json \
51	                                 [--workers ui,docs] --task ui=features/<f>/ui-task.md --task docs=features/<f>/docs-task.md \
52	                                 [--automatic --worker-timeout-seconds N --review-timeout-seconds N --reviewer-transport native|print]
53	$PY -m workflow start     "$RUN" --live [--herdr]
54	```
55	
56	| Action | Required flags | Optional flags | What it does |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `preflight` | `--policy` | `--repo`, `--herdr`, `--automatic` | validates the policy, clean source, installed `git`/`claude`/`node`, the Claude CLI flags the run needs, Claude login; `--herdr` requires a managed Herdr pane (`HERDR_ENV=1`) |
59	| `prepare` | `--policy`, `--task <lane>=<path>` once per selected lane | `--workers a,b`, `--repo`, `--automatic`, the three automatic settings | pins base commit, branch, policy digest, `workers` (selected lanes in declared order) and `excluded_workers` into `plan.json`, creates one worktree per selected lane, writes the first `run-state.json`; `--automatic` requires a `feature/` branch |
60	| `start` | `--live` | `--herdr` | launches every selected lane's native session once; refuses an already-started run; with `--herdr` opens the workflow tab (one pane per lane, in declared order) |
61	
62	Manual-mode gates after the workers finish:
63	
64	```bash
65	$PY -m workflow freeze  "$RUN" --handoff ui=ui-handoff.json --handoff docs=docs-handoff.json   # one --handoff per selected lane
66	$PY -m workflow review  "$RUN" --review-file independent-review.json
67	$PY -m workflow approve "$RUN" --bundle-sha256 <hash printed at the approval interrupt>
68	```
69	
70	| Action | Required flags | What it does |
71	| --- | --- | --- |
72	| `freeze` | `--handoff <lane>=<path>` for every selected lane (each `{"summary": "...", "open_assumptions": []}`) | validates every handoff, stops the recorded sessions, snapshots (an edit under an excluded lane's owned paths is an ownership violation naming both lanes), checks each lane, builds the candidate from the selected lanes in declared order and rechecks it |
73	| `review` | `--review-file` (the review JSON in RUNBOOK section 5) | imports an independent review bound to the exact bundle hash and candidate commit |
74	| `approve` | `--bundle-sha256` | fast-forwards the source branch locally to the reviewed candidate; no push |
75	
76	## 3. Automatic mode
77	
78	```bash
79	$PY -m workflow automatic      "$RUN" --live     # supervise to a verified feature branch, or resume an interrupted run
80	$PY -m workflow automatic-step "$RUN" --live     # one controller step, exit 75 = checkpoint persisted, run again
81	```
82	
83	Resume after Ctrl-C, a closed terminal or a dropped SSH session with the same `automatic --live`; workers and the reviewer keep running meanwhile. Do not repeat `launch` for an existing run. A run stopped by a deadline, a blocked worker, a quota block, a rejected completion file or a blocked review is retained but not resumable: start a new `--run-id`.
84	
85	## 4. Inspect
86	
87	```bash
88	$PY -m workflow status "$RUN"                        # next nodes, pending interrupts, errors; refreshes report.html
89	$PY -m workflow export "$RUN"                        # rebuild run-state.json at the current export version (1.3.0), launches nothing
90	$PY -m workflow attach "$RUN"                        # create the run's Herdr tab and panes when start ran without --herdr
91	$PY -m workflow.interactive status     "$RUN"        # native session inventory for the run
92	$PY -m workflow.interactive attach     "$RUN" [--reuse-observers observers.json]
93	$PY -m workflow.interactive attach-one "$RUN" --node <lane>|review    # reconnect one session in this terminal
94	```
95	
96	`status` prints the run's `workers` and `excluded_workers` with the pending nodes. `attach-one` needs an interactive terminal, accepts any lane of the run or `review`, and refuses to restart a missing session. `export` takes the controller lock, constructs no sessions, and refuses a run whose `plan.json`, policy or `review.json` fail validation. Run it on runs recorded before export 1.3.0 so the viewer shows their review and inputs; an old run keeps its stored graph labels and reports both legacy lanes as selected.
97	
98	## 5. Recovery
99	
100	```bash
101	$PY -m workflow retry     "$RUN" --phase worker    --node docs      # rerun one failed lane check at the same revision
102	$PY -m workflow retry     "$RUN" --phase candidate --node ui        # rerun one failed combined check
103	$PY -m workflow retry     "$RUN"                                    # resume failed post-freeze graph steps, never relaunches
104	$PY -m workflow reconcile "$RUN"                                    # rebind surviving sessions after an ambiguous launch, never relaunches
105	```
106	
107	| Flag | Values | Default |
108	| --- | --- | --- |
109	| `--phase` | `worker`, `candidate` | `worker` |
110	| `--node` | any lane of the run (`workers` in `plan.json`) | none, meaning resume without selecting a check |
111	
112	Three verification attempts per lane and phase, including the first. `retry` refuses runs that are waiting at an interrupt and refuses to relaunch failed `launch_*` steps; use `reconcile` for those.
113	
114	Native session controls, from the run's receipts:
115	
116	```bash
117	claude agents --json                                  # list sessions; the run's are named workflow-<run-id>-<lane> and workflow-<run-id>-reviewer
118	claude stop <background_id>                           # stop one session by its exact id from <node>.interactive.json
119	cd "$RUN/review-worktree" && claude --resume <uuid>   # reread or continue the reviewer transcript
120	```
121	
122	## 6. Viewer
123	
124	```bash
125	npm run dev                                              # API on 127.0.0.1:3001 plus Vite on 127.0.0.1:5173
126	MD_MANAGER_API_PORT=3010 npm run dev:api                 # API alone on another port
127	```
128	
129	The Projects viewer reads registered run roots from the projects registry file named by `MD_MANAGER_PROJECTS_CONFIG`; `config/projects.example.json` shows the shape. Unset means no projects. Sources come from `MD_MANAGER_CONFIG`. The adapter accepts exports 1.0.0 to 1.3.0 and derives the run's lanes from `inputs.workers` (the fixed `ui`/`adapter` pair for exports without `inputs`).
130	
131	## 7. Files in a run directory
132	
133	| File | Written by | Meaning |
134	| --- | --- | --- |
135	| `plan.json`, `policy.json` | `prepare` | pinned base commit, branch, `workers`, `excluded_workers`, `failure_drill`, tasks, automatic settings, policy |
136	| `run-state.json` | every CLI boundary, `export` | versioned export the viewer reads |
137	| `worktree-<lane>/` | `prepare` | one worktree per selected lane |
138	| `<lane\|review>.interactive.json` | launch | session receipt with UUID, launch token, status |
139	| `<node>.prompt.txt`, `<node>.launch.log` | launch | exact prompt and launch output |
140	| `<lane>.completion.json` | the worker | automatic mode completion signal |
141	| `<lane>.handoff.json` | `freeze` or the controller | accepted handoff |
142	| `<node>.stop.json` | stop | identity-checked stop marker |
143	| `review-bundle.json`, `review.diff`, `review-worktree/` | candidate | what the reviewer sees |
144	| `review.completion.json` | the reviewer | bound verdict file |
145	| `automatic-review.json`, `review.json` | controller | review status, accepted verdict and findings |
146	| `verification/<phase>/<node>/<attempt>/packet.json` | checks | check evidence and screenshots |
147	| `report.html`, `events.jsonl`, `terminals.json` | controller | local report, timeline, Herdr pane map |
148	| `controller.lock`, `pipeline.sqlite` | controller | lock and LangGraph checkpoint |
149	
150	## 8. Adding a feature to launch
151	
152	1. Create `features/<name>/` with `feature.json` matching `contracts/workflow/feature.schema.json` (`version` 2.0.0, `name`, `branch_prefix`, `policy`, `workers: [{node_id, task}]`, one entry per lane), `policy.json` matching `contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json` (1.2.0: the same lane ids, a free `role` label, `owned_paths`, `checks` and `required_check_kinds` per lane; lane ids match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and avoid `review`, `candidate`, `handoff`, `approval`, `integrate`, `multiple`, `none`, `both` and the `launch_`/`verify_`/`candidate_`/`review-` prefixes), and one task file per lane.
153	2. Add `<name>` to the `FEATURES` tuple in `workflow/launch.py`.
154	3. `$PY -m workflow launch <name> --dry-run --automatic` until it validates, then `--live`.
155

Every command below was taken from the argparse definitions in `workflow/pipeline.py`, `workflow/launch.py` and `workflow/interactive.py` after the worker-lanes slice (PRD_WORKER_LANES). Longer explanations live in [RUNBOOK.md](RUNBOOK.md) and [features/project-workflows/README.md](../features/project-workflows/README.md).

Worker lanes come from the feature's configuration: `features/<f>/feature.json` (2.0.0) declares every lane with its task file, `features/<f>/policy.json` (1.2.0) gives each lane its role label, owned paths, checks and `required_check_kinds`. A run launches every declared lane or the subset named with `--workers`; `<lane>` below is any selected lane id.

```bash
PY="$PWD/.venv/bin/python"                                   # controller interpreter, run from the repo root
RUN="$HOME/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>/<run-id>"   # run directory, always outside the repo
```

Two entry points:

| Entry point | Shape | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$PY -m workflow launch <feature> [flags]` | one command | prepare and start a committed feature |
| `$PY -m workflow <action> "$RUN" [flags]` | one action per call | every other pipeline step, status, recovery |

Nothing launches a Claude session without `--live`. Nothing ever pushes or merges `main`.

## 1. One-command launch

```bash
$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --dry-run --automatic          # validate and print the commands, execute nothing
$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --live --automatic             # unattended run to a verified feature branch
$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --live                         # manual run with operator gates
$PY -m workflow launch project-workflows --live --automatic --workers adapter   # only the named lanes; the rest stay off-limits
```

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<feature>` | a directory under `features/` listed in `FEATURES` in `workflow/launch.py` | required |
| `--run-id ID` | opaque run identifier, not a path | `<feature>-001` |
| `--run-root DIR` | run storage outside the repository | `~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>` |
| `--workers a,b` | launch only these declared lanes (unknown ids, duplicates and an empty list are refused before any Git action); the selection is pinned in `plan.json` | every declared lane |
| `--live` | authorize Claude usage | off |
| `--automatic` | run-scoped permission bypass for workers, automatic freeze, checks, native reviewer, verified feature branch | off, manual gates |
| `--worker-timeout-seconds N` | per-worker deadline from launch to completion signal, automatic only | 4 h, max 24 h |
| `--review-timeout-seconds N` | reviewer deadline from its launch to its completion file, automatic only | 30 min, max 24 h |
| `--reviewer-transport native\|print` | attachable reviewer session, or headless `claude --print`, automatic only | `native` |
| `--no-herdr` | omit terminal attachments | attaches |
| `--dry-run` | validate the feature configuration and print the commands | off |

`launch` refuses an existing run directory. It runs, in order: `preflight`, `git switch -c <branch_prefix>/<run-id>`, `prepare`, `start`, and with `--automatic` also `automatic`. A `feature.json` still at version 1.0.0 (`ui_task`/`adapter_task`) is translated to the 2.0.0 shape and a deprecation line is printed; `--dry-run` lists it under `notes`. A policy `failure_drill` that names a lane the selection leaves out is skipped, with a note and a timeline event.

## 2. Step-by-step pipeline (what `launch` runs for you)

```bash
$PY -m workflow preflight "$RUN" --repo "$PWD" --policy features/<f>/policy.json --herdr [--automatic]
$PY -m workflow prepare   "$RUN" --repo "$PWD" --policy features/<f>/policy.json \
                                 [--workers ui,docs] --task ui=features/<f>/ui-task.md --task docs=features/<f>/docs-task.md \
                                 [--automatic --worker-timeout-seconds N --review-timeout-seconds N --reviewer-transport native|print]
$PY -m workflow start     "$RUN" --live [--herdr]
```

| Action | Required flags | Optional flags | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preflight` | `--policy` | `--repo`, `--herdr`, `--automatic` | validates the policy, clean source, installed `git`/`claude`/`node`, the Claude CLI flags the run needs, Claude login; `--herdr` requires a managed Herdr pane (`HERDR_ENV=1`) |
| `prepare` | `--policy`, `--task <lane>=<path>` once per selected lane | `--workers a,b`, `--repo`, `--automatic`, the three automatic settings | pins base commit, branch, policy digest, `workers` (selected lanes in declared order) and `excluded_workers` into `plan.json`, creates one worktree per selected lane, writes the first `run-state.json`; `--automatic` requires a `feature/` branch |
| `start` | `--live` | `--herdr` | launches every selected lane's native session once; refuses an already-started run; with `--herdr` opens the workflow tab (one pane per lane, in declared order) |

Manual-mode gates after the workers finish:

```bash
$PY -m workflow freeze  "$RUN" --handoff ui=ui-handoff.json --handoff docs=docs-handoff.json   # one --handoff per selected lane
$PY -m workflow review  "$RUN" --review-file independent-review.json
$PY -m workflow approve "$RUN" --bundle-sha256 <hash printed at the approval interrupt>
```

| Action | Required flags | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `freeze` | `--handoff <lane>=<path>` for every selected lane (each `{"summary": "...", "open_assumptions": []}`) | validates every handoff, stops the recorded sessions, snapshots (an edit under an excluded lane's owned paths is an ownership violation naming both lanes), checks each lane, builds the candidate from the selected lanes in declared order and rechecks it |
| `review` | `--review-file` (the review JSON in RUNBOOK section 5) | imports an independent review bound to the exact bundle hash and candidate commit |
| `approve` | `--bundle-sha256` | fast-forwards the source branch locally to the reviewed candidate; no push |

## 3. Automatic mode

```bash
$PY -m workflow automatic      "$RUN" --live     # supervise to a verified feature branch, or resume an interrupted run
$PY -m workflow automatic-step "$RUN" --live     # one controller step, exit 75 = checkpoint persisted, run again
```

Resume after Ctrl-C, a closed terminal or a dropped SSH session with the same `automatic --live`; workers and the reviewer keep running meanwhile. Do not repeat `launch` for an existing run. A run stopped by a deadline, a blocked worker, a quota block, a rejected completion file or a blocked review is retained but not resumable: start a new `--run-id`.

## 4. Inspect

```bash
$PY -m workflow status "$RUN"                        # next nodes, pending interrupts, errors; refreshes report.html
$PY -m workflow export "$RUN"                        # rebuild run-state.json at the current export version (1.3.0), launches nothing
$PY -m workflow attach "$RUN"                        # create the run's Herdr tab and panes when start ran without --herdr
$PY -m workflow.interactive status     "$RUN"        # native session inventory for the run
$PY -m workflow.interactive attach     "$RUN" [--reuse-observers observers.json]
$PY -m workflow.interactive attach-one "$RUN" --node <lane>|review    # reconnect one session in this terminal
```

`status` prints the run's `workers` and `excluded_workers` with the pending nodes. `attach-one` needs an interactive terminal, accepts any lane of the run or `review`, and refuses to restart a missing session. `export` takes the controller lock, constructs no sessions, and refuses a run whose `plan.json`, policy or `review.json` fail validation. Run it on runs recorded before export 1.3.0 so the viewer shows their review and inputs; an old run keeps its stored graph labels and reports both legacy lanes as selected.

## 5. Recovery

```bash
$PY -m workflow retry     "$RUN" --phase worker    --node docs      # rerun one failed lane check at the same revision
$PY -m workflow retry     "$RUN" --phase candidate --node ui        # rerun one failed combined check
$PY -m workflow retry     "$RUN"                                    # resume failed post-freeze graph steps, never relaunches
$PY -m workflow reconcile "$RUN"                                    # rebind surviving sessions after an ambiguous launch, never relaunches
```

| Flag | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--phase` | `worker`, `candidate` | `worker` |
| `--node` | any lane of the run (`workers` in `plan.json`) | none, meaning resume without selecting a check |

Three verification attempts per lane and phase, including the first. `retry` refuses runs that are waiting at an interrupt and refuses to relaunch failed `launch_*` steps; use `reconcile` for those.

Native session controls, from the run's receipts:

```bash
claude agents --json                                  # list sessions; the run's are named workflow-<run-id>-<lane> and workflow-<run-id>-reviewer
claude stop <background_id>                           # stop one session by its exact id from <node>.interactive.json
cd "$RUN/review-worktree" && claude --resume <uuid>   # reread or continue the reviewer transcript
```

## 6. Viewer

```bash
npm run dev                                              # API on 127.0.0.1:3001 plus Vite on 127.0.0.1:5173
MD_MANAGER_API_PORT=3010 npm run dev:api                 # API alone on another port
```

The Projects viewer reads registered run roots from the projects registry file named by `MD_MANAGER_PROJECTS_CONFIG`; `config/projects.example.json` shows the shape. Unset means no projects. Sources come from `MD_MANAGER_CONFIG`. The adapter accepts exports 1.0.0 to 1.3.0 and derives the run's lanes from `inputs.workers` (the fixed `ui`/`adapter` pair for exports without `inputs`).

## 7. Files in a run directory

| File | Written by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan.json`, `policy.json` | `prepare` | pinned base commit, branch, `workers`, `excluded_workers`, `failure_drill`, tasks, automatic settings, policy |
| `run-state.json` | every CLI boundary, `export` | versioned export the viewer reads |
| `worktree-<lane>/` | `prepare` | one worktree per selected lane |
| `<lane\|review>.interactive.json` | launch | session receipt with UUID, launch token, status |
| `<node>.prompt.txt`, `<node>.launch.log` | launch | exact prompt and launch output |
| `<lane>.completion.json` | the worker | automatic mode completion signal |
| `<lane>.handoff.json` | `freeze` or the controller | accepted handoff |
| `<node>.stop.json` | stop | identity-checked stop marker |
| `review-bundle.json`, `review.diff`, `review-worktree/` | candidate | what the reviewer sees |
| `review.completion.json` | the reviewer | bound verdict file |
| `automatic-review.json`, `review.json` | controller | review status, accepted verdict and findings |
| `verification/<phase>/<node>/<attempt>/packet.json` | checks | check evidence and screenshots |
| `report.html`, `events.jsonl`, `terminals.json` | controller | local report, timeline, Herdr pane map |
| `controller.lock`, `pipeline.sqlite` | controller | lock and LangGraph checkpoint |

## 8. Adding a feature to launch

1. Create `features/<name>/` with `feature.json` matching `contracts/workflow/feature.schema.json` (`version` 2.0.0, `name`, `branch_prefix`, `policy`, `workers: [{node_id, task}]`, one entry per lane), `policy.json` matching `contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json` (1.2.0: the same lane ids, a free `role` label, `owned_paths`, `checks` and `required_check_kinds` per lane; lane ids match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and avoid `review`, `candidate`, `handoff`, `approval`, `integrate`, `multiple`, `none`, `both` and the `launch_`/`verify_`/`candidate_`/`review-` prefixes), and one task file per lane.
2. Add `<name>` to the `FEATURES` tuple in `workflow/launch.py`.
3. `$PY -m workflow launch <name> --dry-run --automatic` until it validates, then `--live`.

185:### Automatic mode: the review step
187:In an automatic run the review node launches the reviewer itself, once per bundle, and waits for its verdict exactly as it waits for worker completion signals:
189:- **Native reviewer session (default).** `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer` starts in `$RUN/review-worktree/` (a detached checkout of the candidate commit) with tools Read, Glob, Grep and Write, permission mode `dontAsk`, no MCP servers, the run directory added as a readable path, and a single allowed write: `$RUN/review.completion.json`. The receipt is `review.interactive.json` (same keys as a worker receipt plus `candidate_commit`), the prompt is kept in `review.prompt.txt`, the launch output in `review.launch.log`. Its session UUID is recorded in the timeline (`Reviewer session <uuid> launched; awaiting review.completion.json`) and must differ from both worker UUIDs.
190:- **Reviewer pane.** When the run's Herdr tab exists, a `Claude: reviewer` pane is split to the right of the last lane's pane and attaches with `attach-one --node review`. You can answer a question the reviewer asks there, exactly as for workers; the transcript is the record, the verdict is only the file. A missing pane never fails the review; `python -m workflow.interactive attach-one "$RUN" --node review` reconnects in any available terminal, and `attach` adds the pane when the reviewer already exists, also to a workflow tab whose worker panes were attached earlier.
191:- **Completion protocol.** The reviewer writes `review.completion.json` once, as its last action, then ends its turn. The controller accepts the file only when it validates against `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`, its `run_id`, `node_id: "review"`, `launch_token`, `bundle_sha256` and `candidate_commit` match the run, the session is `idle` or `done`, the reviewer identity is unchanged and independent, and the review worktree, bundle and `review.diff` hashes are unchanged. Findings carry `worker` (a selected lane id, `multiple` or `none`; the prompt spells out this run's vocabulary, and the print fallback's structured-output schema is generated from it) and `requirement`. Any rejected file, including one naming a lane the run did not select, blocks the run with the reason in `automatic-review.json`; nothing is relaunched.
192:- **Verdict.** `review.json` is written for every verdict. `approved` with no unresolved P0/P1 finding continues to the verified feature branch; `blocked`, or an approval that still carries an unresolved P0/P1 (recorded as `verdict: "blocked"` with the reviewer's raw decision kept in `automatic-review.json`), ends the run. Fixing findings means a new run with a new bundle.
193:- **Deadline.** `review_timeout_seconds` counts from the reviewer's launch (`launch_requested_at`) and survives controller restarts. A reviewer that idles without a file until the deadline blocks the run; **no second reviewer is ever launched**.
194:- **Stop.** After acceptance or a block the controller stops the reviewer with the same identity re-check as for workers (`review.stop.json`); the transcript stays resumable. A stop that cannot be confirmed after acceptance ends the controller with the verdict kept (`automatic-review.json` stays `succeeded`, `review.stop.json` absent or unconfirmed, the reason on the timeline); `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` retries the stop before continuing and launches nothing.
195:- **Interruption.** Ctrl-C, a closed terminal or a dropped SSH session while the controller waits leaves the reviewer running with `automatic-review.json` at `running`; `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` resumes waiting for the same session's file. The same holds inside the launch window once `claude --bg` was issued (`review.interactive.json` exists): the receipt is `running`, without `session_id` when the interrupt hit the settle poll, and resume first binds that one session through reconciliation, never a relaunch. An interrupt before the launch was issued leaves `needs_reconciliation`.
196:- **Print fallback.** `--reviewer-transport print` (at `launch` or `prepare`, pinned into `plan.automatic`) keeps the headless `claude --print --json-schema` reviewer: no pane, no human input, `review.stdout.json`/`review.stderr.log`, the same bundle binding and verdict rules. Plans pinned before the setting existed validate as `native` (they never launch a new reviewer); their exported inputs report the transport their recorded review used, or null.

27:This performs preflight, creates a feature branch (not main), prepares one worktree per selected lane, starts the interactive workers with run-scoped permission bypass/Bash access, and supervises them through checks and independent automated review. Add `--workers ui` (or any comma-separated subset of the declared lanes) to run only those lanes: the others are not launched, their owned paths stay off-limits to every running lane, and the candidate is built from the selected lanes only. The command remains running until it stops on a verified feature branch or a blocker. It never pushes or merges main. Use `--dry-run` instead of `--live` to inspect without execution. Omit `--automatic` for the original manual gates. See the feature README for completion signals, recovery and privilege boundaries. The later features `review-result` and `run-inputs` launch the same way (`features/<feature>/README.md`); `--run-id` defaults to `<feature>-001` and the run root to `~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>`.
29:The profile includes a deliberate first adapter-verification gate failure and a hard limit of three verification attempts per lane/phase. Read the feature README for the exact retry and evidence procedure. Automatic mode adds persisted per-worker deadlines (default 4 hours, `--worker-timeout-seconds`) enforced by the running supervisor and a reviewer deadline (default 30 minutes, `--review-timeout-seconds`, counted from the reviewer's launch). Interrupting the supervisor leaves the workers running and the run resumable; only deadline expiry or a blocked worker stops them. It does not impose token caps or automatically repair code. Manual mode retains operator-controlled worker lifetimes. The independent review runs as a third native session by default; `--reviewer-transport print` keeps the headless `claude --print` reviewer for environments without Herdr (see "Automatic mode: the review step").
33:- One implementation worker per selected lane, as many lanes as the feature declares; each is a native interactive Claude background terminal in its own worktree. A dedicated Herdr tab attaches every terminal with keyboard input enabled: the first lane takes the root pane, each following lane splits right of the previous one, the reviewer splits right of the last lane.
34:- Exact shared starting Git revision is recorded and verified. Frozen ownership is checked against actual captured files, not just agent reports, against the full declared policy: a selected lane that edits a path owned by an excluded lane is an ownership violation naming both lanes. Lane ids follow `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and never take a reserved graph name (`review`, `candidate`, `handoff`, `approval`, `integrate`, `multiple`, `none`, `both`, or a `launch_`/`verify_`/`candidate_`/`review-` prefix). `role` is a free label; each lane's `required_check_kinds` decide which check kinds it must pass (policies before 1.2.0 derive them from the role: `frontend` needs `build` and `browser`, `backend` needs `unit`), so relabelling a lane cannot bypass required tests.
39:- Review is performed by Pi/a fresh reviewer or a human against the exact bundle and candidate. The CLI imports that review; it does not spawn an unconfigured Pi model or fabricate independent review. Review identity is an operator attestation, not a cryptographic identity service.
41:- This is a trusted local development tool, not a sandbox or multi-tenant service. Tests/configuration are executable code. Review policy commands and task ownership before approving a run. CLI/manual terminal input is trusted operator authority.

183:Review does not integrate. The graph then waits at a separate approval interrupt.
185:### Automatic mode: the review step
187:In an automatic run the review node launches the reviewer itself, once per bundle, and waits for its verdict exactly as it waits for worker completion signals:
189:- **Native reviewer session (default).** `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer` starts in `$RUN/review-worktree/` (a detached checkout of the candidate commit) with tools Read, Glob, Grep and Write, permission mode `dontAsk`, no MCP servers, the run directory added as a readable path, and a single allowed write: `$RUN/review.completion.json`. The receipt is `review.interactive.json` (same keys as a worker receipt plus `candidate_commit`), the prompt is kept in `review.prompt.txt`, the launch output in `review.launch.log`. Its session UUID is recorded in the timeline (`Reviewer session <uuid> launched; awaiting review.completion.json`) and must differ from both worker UUIDs.
190:- **Reviewer pane.** When the run's Herdr tab exists, a `Claude: reviewer` pane is split to the right of the last lane's pane and attaches with `attach-one --node review`. You can answer a question the reviewer asks there, exactly as for workers; the transcript is the record, the verdict is only the file. A missing pane never fails the review; `python -m workflow.interactive attach-one "$RUN" --node review` reconnects in any available terminal, and `attach` adds the pane when the reviewer already exists, also to a workflow tab whose worker panes were attached earlier.
191:- **Completion protocol.** The reviewer writes `review.completion.json` once, as its last action, then ends its turn. The controller accepts the file only when it validates against `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`, its `run_id`, `node_id: "review"`, `launch_token`, `bundle_sha256` and `candidate_commit` match the run, the session is `idle` or `done`, the reviewer identity is unchanged and independent, and the review worktree, bundle and `review.diff` hashes are unchanged. Findings carry `worker` (a selected lane id, `multiple` or `none`; the prompt spells out this run's vocabulary, and the print fallback's structured-output schema is generated from it) and `requirement`. Any rejected file, including one naming a lane the run did not select, blocks the run with the reason in `automatic-review.json`; nothing is relaunched.
192:- **Verdict.** `review.json` is written for every verdict. `approved` with no unresolved P0/P1 finding continues to the verified feature branch; `blocked`, or an approval that still carries an unresolved P0/P1 (recorded as `verdict: "blocked"` with the reviewer's raw decision kept in `automatic-review.json`), ends the run. Fixing findings means a new run with a new bundle.
193:- **Deadline.** `review_timeout_seconds` counts from the reviewer's launch (`launch_requested_at`) and survives controller restarts. A reviewer that idles without a file until the deadline blocks the run; **no second reviewer is ever launched**.
194:- **Stop.** After acceptance or a block the controller stops the reviewer with the same identity re-check as for workers (`review.stop.json`); the transcript stays resumable. A stop that cannot be confirmed after acceptance ends the controller with the verdict kept (`automatic-review.json` stays `succeeded`, `review.stop.json` absent or unconfirmed, the reason on the timeline); `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` retries the stop before continuing and launches nothing.
195:- **Interruption.** Ctrl-C, a closed terminal or a dropped SSH session while the controller waits leaves the reviewer running with `automatic-review.json` at `running`; `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` resumes waiting for the same session's file. The same holds inside the launch window once `claude --bg` was issued (`review.interactive.json` exists): the receipt is `running`, without `session_id` when the interrupt hit the settle poll, and resume first binds that one session through reconciliation, never a relaunch. An interrupt before the launch was issued leaves `needs_reconciliation`.
196:- **Print fallback.** `--reviewer-transport print` (at `launch` or `prepare`, pinned into `plan.automatic`) keeps the headless `claude --print --json-schema` reviewer: no pane, no human input, `review.stdout.json`/`review.stderr.log`, the same bundle binding and verdict rules. Plans pinned before the setting existed validate as `native` (they never launch a new reviewer); their exported inputs report the transport their recorded review used, or null.

201:cd "$RUN/review-worktree" && claude --resume <reviewer-uuid>

15:Workers emit an explicit run/node/token-bound completion file. Idle alone is insufficient. The controller freezes completed work, executes the real isolated and combined checks, and launches a fresh read-only Claude reviewer from the LangGraph review node: by default a third native session (`workflow-<run>-reviewer` in `review-worktree/`, tools Read/Glob/Grep plus a single allowed write of `review.completion.json`) with its own `Claude: reviewer` pane in the run's tab, or a headless `claude --print` job with `--reviewer-transport print`. The reviewer reports its verdict only through a completion file bound to the run, launch token, bundle hash and candidate commit, validated against `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`; the review is bound to the exact candidate and evidence hash. Only a passing review permits fast-forwarding the newly created `feature/…` branch. **No merge to main and no push.**
19:Bounds: per-worker deadlines measured from launch to completion signal (default 4 hours, `--worker-timeout-seconds`, at most 24 hours; persisted launch times survive restart and are enforced only while the supervisor is running), a reviewer process timeout (default 30 minutes, `--review-timeout-seconds`), existing per-check timeouts, three check attempts per lane/phase and at most 45 controller-step processes per supervisor invocation. There is no token cap or billing/provider fallback. Ambiguous launches, missing completion signals, quota blocks, reviewer rejection, ownership violations and exhausted retries stop with retained evidence. Review/worker processes are not blindly relaunched. A stopped/crashed controller cannot enforce process deadlines while it is offline.
21:These retries rerun verification of immutable code; they are **not** an automatic source-repair loop. Persistent code failures or review findings require intervention. Fully automatic means no routine approval prompts on the successful path, not a guarantee that every run succeeds.
31:Do not repeat `launch` for an existing run. Uncertain launches still require explicit reconciliation. New files include `<lane>.completion.json` and `<lane>.prompt.txt` for every selected lane (the exact prompt each native session received), `automatic-review.json`, `review.diff` and the isolated `review-worktree/`. The native reviewer adds `review.interactive.json` (launch receipt with the reviewer's session UUID), `review.prompt.txt`, `review.launch.log`, `review.completion.json` (the reviewer's bound verdict file) and `review.stop.json` (the identity-checked stop); the print fallback keeps `review.stdout.json` and `review.stderr.log`. The reviewer has Read/Glob/Grep and, natively, Write of its completion file only; no shell or edit tools. Interrupting the controller while it waits for the reviewer leaves the reviewer running and `automatic --live` resumes it; a reviewer that never writes its file blocks the run at `review_timeout_seconds`, and no second reviewer is launched. Synthetic tests of this path are not live Claude validation.
47:**Starting is one command; finishing is supervised.** Watch the Claude panes and answer permission prompts. When every worker finishes, return to Pi to collect handoffs (`freeze --handoff <lane>=<path>` per lane), freeze, review and approve. The start command returns at the handoff checkpoint rather than waiting forever or treating idle as completion. A separately started CLI process does not automatically wake this Pi chat.
74:The single-node definition above illustrates shape, not the full production DAG. Use `graph_nodes(lanes)` from `workflow/export_state.py` for the pipeline definition of a given lane list (for this feature, `["ui", "adapter"]`). Tests may register a smaller valid graph. Project/workflow IDs are unique within their scope. Paths must be operator-supplied absolute canonical directories; never derive registrations from browser parameters or a run's `plan.repository` value. Reject overlapping/ambiguous run registrations. `repository` may differ from `runs_root` (real pipeline data lives outside the repo).
76:Current definitions come from registry configuration. Each run's pinned definition comes from its persisted export, not the current registry definition. Public definitions add scope/version and compute the definition hash as specified in the project API contract.
80:The controller now writes **`run-state.json` atomically** during preparation and each CLI reporting boundary. The adapter must read this file, not launch Python or decode the checkpoint database. Export version 1.0.0 contains:
82:- `run_id`, `base_commit`, stable `created_at`, persisted `updated_at` (unchanged exports do not bump it).
84:- `values`: LangGraph state; completed launch receipts at `ui`/`adapter`, frozen `snapshots`, successful `ui_packet`/`adapter_packet` paths, candidate `bundle`, accepted `review`, `approved_bundle`, and final `integrated_commit` as stages complete (from export 1.3.0 the per-lane receipts and packet paths live under `lanes.<lane>` and `packets.<lane>` instead).
92:**Export version 1.2.0** (`workflow/export_state.py`) keeps everything above unchanged and adds two keys; the adapter accepts `1.0.0` (neither key), `1.1.0` (`review` only), `1.2.0` (both) and `1.3.0` (both, lanes from configuration; see below). Each is an object or `null`, derived read-only from the run's own files; a missing file is `null` and a malformed optional receipt is `null`, never a guess:
94:- `review` (`null` unless `review.json` exists): `attempt` (1), `transport` (`native` when `review.interactive.json` exists, else `print` when `automatic-review.json` exists, else `manual`), `reviewer_session_id` (`review.json` `reviewer`: the Claude session UUID or the operator-stated identity), `independent`, `bundle_sha256`, `candidate_commit`, `verdict` (`approved`/`blocked`), `findings[]` with `severity`, `message`, `disposition`, `worker` (`ui|adapter|both|none` or `null`) and `requirement` (verbatim quote or `null`; both `null` for reviews recorded before the reviewer prompt asked for them), `reviewed_at` (`automatic-review.json` `accepted_at`, else the last `review` event time, else the mtime of `review.json`; UTC with a trailing `Z`), and `diff` (`{path: "review.diff", sha256, bytes}` or `null`).
95:- `inputs` (`null` when `policy.json` is missing): `feature`, `policy_version`, `base_commit`, `source_branch`, `mode` (`automatic` iff `plan.json` has `automatic`), `automatic` (`{finish, permission_mode, worker_timeout_seconds, review_timeout_seconds, reviewer_transport}` or `null`; for plans that predate `reviewer_transport` the export records the transport a recorded review actually used, `native` or `print`, and `null` when no review has happened, never a default), `setup[]` (`{argv, command, timeout_seconds}` with `command = shlex.join(argv)`), `max_verification_attempts`, `failure_drill`, and `workers.<lane>` (keyed by the selected lanes in policy order): `role`, `task` (the plan's task text verbatim, including the appended ownership/checks JSON), `prompt` (`<worker>.prompt.txt` or `null` when the run did not record it), `owned_paths`, `checks[]` (`{id, kind, argv, command, timeout_seconds, scenarios}`), `launch` (the `<worker>.interactive.json` receipt: `session_id`, `launch_token`, `launch_requested_at` normalised to `Z`, `native_started_at` epoch ms, `observed_state`, `status`, `launcher_invocations`, `background_id`; or `null`), `completion` (`<worker>.completion.json` reduced to `{status, summary, open_assumptions}` or `null`), `handoff` (`{summary, open_assumptions}` or `null`) and `stop` (`{stopped, confirmed_at}` where `confirmed_at` is the stop file's mtime when stopped, else `null`).
97:**Export version 1.3.0** (`EXPORT_VERSION`) is additive: the `definition` has one `launch_<lane>` (label `Launch <lane> worker`) and one `verify_<lane>` (`Verify <lane>`) node per selected lane before the fixed tail; `values.lanes.<lane>` and `values.packets.<lane>` replace the flat `<lane>`/`<lane>_packet` keys; `inputs.workers` is keyed by any lane id and each worker gains `required_check_kinds`; `inputs` gains `selected_workers` and `excluded_workers`; `review.findings[].worker` is a lane id, `multiple` or `none` (the legacy `both` survives only in reviews recorded before 1.3.0). A run recorded before 1.3.0 re-exports with its stored definition unchanged (same node ids and labels), both legacy lanes as `selected_workers`, `required_check_kinds` derived from the roles, and its launch evidence carried under `values.lanes`/`values.packets`. The adapter derives the lane list from `inputs.workers` and the node map from the `launch_<lane>`, `verify_<lane>` and `candidate_<lane>` naming; exports without `inputs` (1.0.0, 1.1.0) fall back to the fixed `ui`/`adapter` pair.
99:Task and prompt texts, finding messages and requirement quotes can contain absolute paths: the adapter redacts them and truncates oversized texts. Runs recorded under an older version keep loading; re-export them so the viewer shows their review and inputs:
102:.venv/bin/python -m workflow export "$HOME/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001"
105:The command takes the controller lock, reads the checkpoint without invoking any node, constructs no sessions, launches nothing, refuses a run whose `plan.json`, pinned policy or `review.json` fail validation, and leaves `updated_at` alone when nothing changed.
107:Internal node IDs and state keys are not identical: `launch_<lane>` completes when `values.<lane>` (before 1.3.0) or `values.lanes.<lane>` exists; `handoff` uses `snapshots`; `verify_<lane>` uses `values.<lane>_packet` or `values.packets.<lane>`; `candidate` uses `bundle`; `review`, `approval`, `integrate` use `review`, `approved_bundle`, `integrated_commit`. Task errors override inferred completion; an interrupt marks its node awaiting approval. Nodes with no progress remain pending. Launch-node success means a session launched, not successful implementation. The graph is succeeded only when integrated with no pending work.
133:This is a new controller process using the same persisted LangGraph thread/checkpoint. Expected: no worker relaunch; successful UI verification reused; adapter verification attempt 2 runs. Record the actual evidence, not only this expectation. `failure-drill.json` preserves pre-retry native identities; `failure-report.json` and the review bundle record post-retry identities and check-attempt directories. Null native launch time/count fields mean unavailable evidence, not a guessed count. Out-of-band manual native restarts are not certified by this report.

### Automatic mode: the review step

In an automatic run the review node launches the reviewer itself, once per bundle, and waits for its verdict exactly as it waits for worker completion signals:

- **Native reviewer session (default).** `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer` starts in `$RUN/review-worktree/` (a detached checkout of the candidate commit) with tools Read, Glob, Grep and Write, permission mode `dontAsk`, no MCP servers, the run directory added as a readable path, and a single allowed write: `$RUN/review.completion.json`. The receipt is `review.interactive.json` (same keys as a worker receipt plus `candidate_commit`), the prompt is kept in `review.prompt.txt`, the launch output in `review.launch.log`. Its session UUID is recorded in the timeline (`Reviewer session <uuid> launched; awaiting review.completion.json`) and must differ from both worker UUIDs.
- **Reviewer pane.** When the run's Herdr tab exists, a `Claude: reviewer` pane is split to the right of the last lane's pane and attaches with `attach-one --node review`. You can answer a question the reviewer asks there, exactly as for workers; the transcript is the record, the verdict is only the file. A missing pane never fails the review; `python -m workflow.interactive attach-one "$RUN" --node review` reconnects in any available terminal, and `attach` adds the pane when the reviewer already exists, also to a workflow tab whose worker panes were attached earlier.
- **Completion protocol.** The reviewer writes `review.completion.json` once, as its last action, then ends its turn. The controller accepts the file only when it validates against `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`, its `run_id`, `node_id: "review"`, `launch_token`, `bundle_sha256` and `candidate_commit` match the run, the session is `idle` or `done`, the reviewer identity is unchanged and independent, and the review worktree, bundle and `review.diff` hashes are unchanged. Findings carry `worker` (a selected lane id, `multiple` or `none`; the prompt spells out this run's vocabulary, and the print fallback's structured-output schema is generated from it) and `requirement`. Any rejected file, including one naming a lane the run did not select, blocks the run with the reason in `automatic-review.json`; nothing is relaunched.
- **Verdict.** `review.json` is written for every verdict. `approved` with no unresolved P0/P1 finding continues to the verified feature branch; `blocked`, or an approval that still carries an unresolved P0/P1 (recorded as `verdict: "blocked"` with the reviewer's raw decision kept in `automatic-review.json`), ends the run. Fixing findings means a new run with a new bundle.
- **Deadline.** `review_timeout_seconds` counts from the reviewer's launch (`launch_requested_at`) and survives controller restarts. A reviewer that idles without a file until the deadline blocks the run; **no second reviewer is ever launched**.
- **Stop.** After acceptance or a block the controller stops the reviewer with the same identity re-check as for workers (`review.stop.json`); the transcript stays resumable. A stop that cannot be confirmed after acceptance ends the controller with the verdict kept (`automatic-review.json` stays `succeeded`, `review.stop.json` absent or unconfirmed, the reason on the timeline); `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` retries the stop before continuing and launches nothing.
- **Interruption.** Ctrl-C, a closed terminal or a dropped SSH session while the controller waits leaves the reviewer running with `automatic-review.json` at `running`; `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` resumes waiting for the same session's file. The same holds inside the launch window once `claude --bg` was issued (`review.interactive.json` exists): the receipt is `running`, without `session_id` when the interrupt hit the settle poll, and resume first binds that one session through reconciliation, never a relaunch. An interrupt before the launch was issued leaves `needs_reconciliation`.
- **Print fallback.** `--reviewer-transport print` (at `launch` or `prepare`, pinned into `plan.automatic`) keeps the headless `claude --print --json-schema` reviewer: no pane, no human input, `review.stdout.json`/`review.stderr.log`, the same bundle binding and verdict rules. Plans pinned before the setting existed validate as `native` (they never launch a new reviewer); their exported inputs report the transport their recorded review used, or null.

```bash

The committed Projects-viewer assignment is in [features/project-workflows](../features/project-workflows/README.md). From a clean checkout in Herdr:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m workflow launch project-workflows --live --automatic
```

This performs preflight, creates a feature branch (not main), prepares one worktree per selected lane, starts the interactive workers with run-scoped permission bypass/Bash access, and supervises them through checks and independent automated review. Add `--workers ui` (or any comma-separated subset of the declared lanes) to run only those lanes: the others are not launched, their owned paths stay off-limits to every running lane, and the candidate is built from the selected lanes only. The command remains running until it stops on a verified feature branch or a blocker. It never pushes or merges main. Use `--dry-run` instead of `--live` to inspect without execution. Omit `--automatic` for the original manual gates. See the feature README for completion signals, recovery and privilege boundaries. The later features `review-result` and `run-inputs` launch the same way (`features/<feature>/README.md`); `--run-id` defaults to `<feature>-001` and the run root to `~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>`.

Interrupting the supervisor leaves the workers running and the run resumable; only deadline expiry or a blocked worker stops them. It does not impose token caps or automatically repair code. ## Guarantees and boundaries

- One implementation worker per selected lane, as many lanes as the feature declares; each is a native interactive Claude background terminal in its own worktree. A dedicated Herdr tab attaches every terminal with keyboard input enabled: the first lane takes the root pane, each following lane splits right of the previous one, the reviewer splits right of the last lane.
- Exact shared starting Git revision is recorded and verified. Frozen ownership is checked against actual captured files, not just agent reports, against the full declared policy: a selected lane that edits a path owned by an excluded lane is an ownership violation naming both lanes. Lane ids follow `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and never take a reserved graph name (`review`, `candidate`, `handoff`, `approval`, `integrate`, `multiple`, `none`, `both`, or a `launch_`/`verify_`/`candidate_`/`review-` prefix). `role` is a free label; each lane's `required_check_kinds` decide which check kinds it must pass (policies before 1.2.0 derive them from the role: `frontend` needs `build` and `browser`, `backend` needs `unit`), so relabelling a lane cannot bypass required tests.
- **Idle is not complete.** The operator gathers handoff summaries/assumptions and explicitly freezes the run. The runtime stops every worker process before snapshotting. Source ownership violations or uncertain termination block capture.
- Verification runs in fresh worktrees, with separate cache, temp, browser-output and artifact directories. Installed Python/Node/browser executables may be shared read-only; do not share mutable dependency installations.
- Each lane runs the checks its policy entry lists and must cover its `required_check_kinds` (for the committed feature: the UI lane builds and runs real Playwright scenarios with a PNG attachment per scenario; the adapter lane runs unit tests plus the configured contract/build checks). Missing tests, skipped required scenarios, flaky browser retries, nonzero exits and missing/tampered artifacts block the graph.
- Every lane's snapshot is checked separately, then the combined integration candidate (the selected lanes cherry-picked in declared order) is checked again per lane. Thus individually passing workers are not sufficient for integration. A run over one lane is valid: its candidate is that lane's snapshot, still verified in the combined phase.
- Review is performed by Pi/a fresh reviewer or a human against the exact bundle and candidate. The CLI imports that review; it does not spawn an unconfigured Pi model or fabricate independent review. Review identity is an operator attestation, not a cryptographic identity service.
- Explicit approval authorizes a **local fast-forward of the original source branch**. Source drift/dirty state blocks it. Nothing pushes, publishes, deletes worktrees, or changes provider/billing plans automatically.
- This is a trusted local development tool, not a sandbox or multi-tenant service. Tests/configuration are executable code. Review policy commands and task ownership before approving a run. CLI/manual terminal input is trusted operator authority.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r workflow/requirements.lock
npm ci
npx --no-install playwright install chromium

.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s workflow -t . -v
